name: India
summary: India has two national stock exchanges in Mumbai: BSE, founded in 1875 and Asia's oldest exchange, and the National Stock Exchange (NSE), which introduced screen-based trading in 1994. The Nifty 50 and the Sensex are the headline indexes. India completed its move to next-day (T+1) settlement in January 2023, more than a year before the US. For foreign private investors, direct access is limited, so most invest through funds.

currency.name: Indian rupee
currency.note: Indian shares are priced in rupees, so a euro investor carries currency risk: moves of the rupee against the euro change the value of holdings in euros (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE)
exchanges.founded: Began operations in 1994 as India's first screen-based exchange
exchanges.hours: Pre-open session 09:00–09:15, continuous trading 09:15–15:30, closing auction matching 15:30–15:35, and a closing session 15:50–16:00.
exchanges.note: India Standard Time is UTC+5:30, a half-hour offset, and India does not use daylight saving time.

exchanges.name: BSE (formerly Bombay Stock Exchange)
exchanges.note: BSE describes itself as Asia's oldest exchange and the world's largest by number of listed companies.

indexes.name: Nifty 50
indexes.description: A free-float market-capitalisation-weighted index of large NSE-listed companies. Base value 1,000 on 3 November 1995, one year after NSE's equity market started. It covered about 54% of the free-float market value of NSE-listed shares in March 2026. Calculated by NSE Indices.

indexes.name: BSE Sensex
indexes.description: India's first stock market index, launched on 2 January 1986. Measures the 30 largest, most liquid companies listed on BSE across key sectors. Base value 100 (base date 3 April 1979).

regulators.name: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
regulators.role: India's securities market regulator: set up in 1988 and a statutory body since the SEBI Act came into force on 30 January 1992.

regulators.name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
regulators.role: Central bank; regulates banks and foreign exchange.

investorProtection.name: Deposit insurance (DICGC)
investorProtection.text: Bank deposits are insured up to ₹5 lakh (₹500,000) per depositor and bank, principal and interest combined. Unchanged since 4 February 2020.

settlement.cycle: T+1 (next business day); optional same-day T+0 for selected shares
settlement.csd: Two depositories: NSDL (National Securities Depository) and CDSL (Central Depository Services)
settlement.note: India moved from T+2 to T+1 in phases from 2021, completed in January 2023. An optional T+0 settlement cycle started on 28 March 2024 for a limited set of shares.

source.title: Consultation paper on optional T+0 settlement, May 2024 (SEBI, PDF)

rules.title: Securities transaction tax (STT)
rules.text: Delivery-based purchases and sales of shares on an Indian exchange each pay 0.1% STT (the buyer on purchases, the seller on sales). Intraday trades pay a lower rate on the sell side.

source.title: SEBI turnover fees, STT and other levies (NSE)

rules.title: Shares are held in electronic (demat) accounts
rules.text: Investors hold Indian shares in a demat account with a depository participant of NSDL or CDSL.

rules.title: Limited direct access for foreigners
rules.text: Foreign investors generally invest in listed Indian shares under SEBI's Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) rules, which require registration through a designated depository participant. Private investors abroad therefore usually use funds or depositary receipts instead.

source.title: Frequently asked questions on the SEBI FPI Regulations, as on 24 June 2026 (NSDL FPI Monitor)

taxes.glance: Listed shares (STT paid): long-term gains (held over 12 months) taxed at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh; short-term gains 20% (rates since 23 July 2024). Dividends paid to non-residents: 20% tax deducted at source, reducible by treaty. STT 0.1% on delivery trades. A new Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026.

items.title: Long-term capital gains
items.text: Gains on listed equity shares held for more than 12 months, where STT was paid, are taxed at 12.5% on the amount above ₹1.25 lakh a year (10% above ₹1 lakh for sales before 23 July 2024).

items.title: Short-term capital gains
items.text: Gains on listed equity shares held for 12 months or less, sold on an exchange with STT paid, are taxed at 20% (15% for sales before 23 July 2024).

items.title: Dividends for non-residents
items.text: Tax is deducted at source at 20% on dividends paid to non-residents. A tax treaty may allow a lower rate.

items.title: New law
items.text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026, with new section numbers. Check current rates with the Income Tax Department.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q); higher Indian tax must be reduced under the treaty or reclaimed in India.

sources.title: Tax on long-term capital gains (Income Tax Department, India)
The Income Tax Act, 2025 to come into effect from 1st April, 2026 (PIB, Government of India)

access: Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on Indian indexes such as the Nifty 50, or on emerging-market indexes (Category H). This is the usual route for private investors in Austria.
Some large Indian companies have depositary receipts listed in the US; check which are available through your bank or broker.
Direct trading on NSE or BSE requires registration under SEBI's foreign investor rules and is rarely offered to private investors abroad.

history.text: The Sensex, India's first stock index, is launched on 2 January.
The SEBI Act comes into force on 30 January, making SEBI a statutory regulator.
NSE starts operations as India's first screen-based exchange.
India completes its move to T+1 settlement in January.
Optional same-day (T+0) settlement starts on 28 March for a limited set of shares.

funFacts: Every year NSE holds a special 'Muhurat' trading session for Diwali, the festival of lights; in 2026 it is on Sunday 8 November.
India's clock runs 5½ hours ahead of UTC, so Vienna is 3½ hours behind Mumbai in summer and 4½ hours in winter.
